Therapeutic potential of drugs targeting lactylation in CVDs

Targeting lactylation in CVDs involves direct and indirect strategies (the preclinical research‐based hypothetical framework). Direct approaches focus on lactylation enzymes: (1) transferases such as p300 (inhibited by C646/A485; activated by CTB) and AARS1 (blocked by β‐alanine); (2) de‐transferases, such as HDACs (inhibited by TSA/SAHA) and SIRTs (modulated by SRT1720/EX527). Indirect approaches target lactate metabolism: (1) lactate transport via MCT1/MCT4 inhibitors (AZD‐3965/VB124) or CHC; (2) lactate production by inhibiting LDH (GNE‐1436/Oxa/FX‐11), HK (2‐DG/PROTAC HK2 Degrader‐1), PKM (DCA/shikonin), or mitochondrial complex I (rotenone). Other agents (dexmedetomidine/Dex, Aloe, A2–4–2–4, andrographolide/AGP) regulate lactylation‐linked pathways to ameliorate CVDs. 2‐DG indicates 2‐deoxy‐D‐glucose; α‐KG, alpha‐ketoglutarate; AARS1, aminoacyl‐tRNA synthetase 1; AGP, alpha‐glycerophosphate; Aloe, Aloe‐emodin; A485, a selective inhibitor of p300/CBP histone acetyltransferase; AZD‐3965, a monocarboxylate transporter 1 inhibitor; C646, a p300/CBP histone acetyltransferase inhibitor; CHC, α‐cyano‐4‐hydroxycinnamate; CTB, cholera toxin B subunit; CVD, cardiovascular disease; CoA, coenzyme A; DCA, dichloroacetate; Dex, dexamethasone; EX527, a selective SIRT1 inhibitor; FX‐11, a lactate dehydrogenase A inhibitor; GNE‐14, a hexokinase II inhibitor; HDAC, histone deacetylase; HK, hexokinase; LA, lactate; LDH, lactate dehydrogenase; LDHA, lactate dehydrogenase A; MCT1, monocarboxylate transporter1; MCT4, monocarboxylate transporter 4; MDH2, malate dehydrogenase 2; Oxa, oxamate; PDH, pyruvate dehydrogenase; PDK, pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase; PROTAC, proteolysis‐targeting chimera; PKM, pyruvate kinase; p300, E1A‐binding protein p300 (a histone acetyltransferase); SAHA, suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid; SIRT, sirtuins (NAD+‐dependent deacetylases); SRIT1720, an SIRT1 activator; TSA, trichostatin A; and VB124, a monocarboxylate transporter 4 inhibitor
